findings: Single-card parity: hipEngine prefill is within 7% and decode within 1.1% of a purpose-tuned RDNA3 llama.cpp fork at the same 512/128 c=1 protocol, at 15% more device memory.
TP2 decode parity: hipEngine TP2 decode (38.79 tok/s) is within 6% of llama.cpp tensor-split decode (41.30 tok/s) and is 1.26x its own single-card decode.

TP2 prefill is the dominant gap: hipEngine TP2 prefill is 39.49 tok/s, 0.045x its own single-card bulk-prefill route and 0.027x llama.cpp's tensor-split prefill. llama.cpp's TP2 prefill scales (1.57x vs its TP1); hipEngine's regresses by 22x. The cause is documented in docs/QWEN38-27B-GFX1100-TP2.md: the TP2 session drives prefill token-by-token and the rank-local bulk prefill plan is not implemented yet.

TP2 does not reduce per-rank residency: hipEngine TP2 uses 22.37 GiB per rank, 1.26x its own single-card footprint, while llama.cpp's tensor split halves per-rank weights to 7.49 GiB (7.75 GiB total per rank). The manifest plans 7.83 GiB of resident weights per rank, so ~14.5 GiB per rank is unexplained by the shard plan and needs a follow-up residency audit.
Capacity consequence: after a TP2 load the 24 GiB RX 7900 XTX rank has 1.58 GiB free, which bounds context growth and explains the tight capacity ladder observed in the 2026-09-18 TP2 artifacts.
next_actions: Implement the rank-local bulk TP2 prefill plan (docs/QWEN38-27B-GFX1100-TP2.md, P1/P2) and re-measure this exact protocol; the prefill cell is where TP2 is currently unusable for long prompts.

Audit TP2 per-rank residency against the shard manifest: identify the ~14.5 GiB per rank that is not planned resident weight, then decide whether the full-model materialization should be released after shard binding.
